related_questions.question: Does max contribution to 401k include employer match?

text_blocks.snippet: No, the maximum employee contribution to a 401(k) does not include the employer's matching contribution. The IRS sets a limit on how much an employee can contribute, and the employer's match is in addition to this limit.

list.title: Employee Contribution Limit:
list.snippet: For 2025, the employee contribution limit is $23,500 if you're under 50 and $31,000 if you're 50 or older (including the catch-up contribution).

list.title: Employer Match:
list.snippet: The employer match is a separate contribution made by your employer, on top of your own contributions.

list.title: Total Contribution Limit:
list.snippet: The total contributions (employee and employer) to a 401(k) cannot exceed $70,000 for 2025, or 100% of your compensation, whichever is less.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: If you contribute $23,500 and your employer matches $5,000, your total contribution is $28,500. However, the total contribution to your 401(k) plan cannot exceed $70,000.

related_questions.question: Can I contribute full $6,000 to IRA if I have a 401k?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can absolutely contribute the full $6,000 (or $7,000 if you're age 50 or older) to an IRA, even if you also contribute to a 401(k). The key is that the contribution limits for each type of account are separate and independent. For 2024 and 2025, the IRA contribution limit is $6,000, increasing to $7,000 for those 50 and older.

list.title: IRA Limits:

list.title: Contribution Types:

list.title: Income Limitations:
